Anti-GBM Disease: Daily, at least 14 days until anti-GBM antibodies 20% of baseline
Small-Vessel Vasculitis: Daily or alternate daily, 7-10 days depending on clinical response
Cryoglobulinemia: At least 7-10 days or until clinical response
Recurrent FSGS After Transplantation: Daily for at least 10 days initially, then continuing less frequently, often for months
HUS/TTP: Daily for 7-10 days or until platelet count 80-100 ×10⁹/L (sometimes needed twice daily)

Anti-GBM Disease: 20 mL 10% calcium gluconate (occasionally more), 3 mL 15% KCl if not dialysis dependent, heparin 2000-5000 U bolus, then 500-2000/h (LMWH an alternative with bolus only) or citrate anticoagulation
HUS/TTP: As for anti-GBM disease (may need more calcium because of increased volume of FFP-containing citrate)

Anti-GBM Disease: FFP 5-8mL/kg at end of exchange volume if hemorrhage risk (kidney biopsy in last 48h, lung hemorrhage, platelets <40×10⁹/L, fibrinogen <1.5g/L) Immunoadsorption may be as effective
Small-Vessel Vasculitis: As for anti-GBM disease Immunoadsorption may be as effective
Recurrent FSGS After Transplantation: As for anti-GBM disease; may need to include replacement immunoglobulins if continuing long term Immunoadsorption may be as effective
